format: F8 Then and Now (layer: F13 Scale Shock)

pills.text: IS INDIA RUNNING OUT OF BABIES?

scenes.vo: In NFHS-4, the twenty fifteen sixteen survey, Bihar's fertility rate was three point four children per woman.
scenes.visual: From frame 0 the uncle stands in a Bihar home beside a mother, the title question and the spelled-out NFHS sit on pills, and a big circled badge lands on the narrator's number: 3.4 children per woman, an average, not a family.

pills.text: AVERAGE PER WOMAN, NOT A FAMILY

scenes.vo: In NFHS-6, the twenty twenty-three twenty-four survey, it is two point seven.
scenes.visual: Same room, same mother and pram, no extra figures: only the badge changes, to 2.7, under pills that say it is an average per woman and that the NFHS-6 sheets are provisional.

scenes.vo: Bihar is still the highest of all the places surveyed.
scenes.visual: The India map fills state by state in the fertility colour scale and Bihar lifts off the map while the others dim.

scenes.vo: In thirty of the thirty-five states and union territories in NFHS-6,
scenes.visual: The uncle points at a big 30, a small pill saying OF and a smaller 35, above a row of five little houses: the count of places, shown as one fraction.

scenes.vo: the rate is at or below two point one, a number demographers call the replacement level.
scenes.visual: The map re-colours in two flat colours, the places at or below the replacement line in cool blue and the few above it in warm orange.

spec.title: Is India running out of babies?

scenes.vo: So what is really happening to India's fertility rate?
scenes.visual: A sunburst title card: the uncle and the film's question in big type, 'Here's the map.' under it.

scenes.vo: The answer depends on where you live, and the map holds some surprises.
scenes.visual: The full fertility map fills in again, a wave from north-west to south-east, with its legend.

scenes.vo: Demographers watch one number above all: the total fertility rate, or TFR.
scenes.visual: A solid blue card with big white type, TFR in yellow, and the uncle peeking up in the corner (the section header).

scenes.vo: It is the average number of children a woman would have by the end of her childbearing years,
scenes.visual: A mother alone at home (no host in this one); a pram pops in on 'children' and a clock on 'end', under the pill AVERAGE CHILDREN PER WOMAN.

scenes.vo: if she had children at the rates measured in the years just before the survey.
scenes.visual: In a clinic a big calendar pops in on 'years' beside the mother, under the pill RATES FROM RECENT YEARS.

pills.text: A SNAPSHOT OF THE RECENT PAST

scenes.vo: So it is a snapshot of the recent past. It is not a count of how many children each family actually has.
scenes.visual: The uncle, now on the right, shows a clock for 'a snapshot', then a family pops in on 'each family' under the pill NOT A HEADCOUNT: the picture of what TFR is not.

scenes.vo: The magic line is two point one. The United Nations says the replacement level is about two point one children per woman:
scenes.visual: Two parent figures, an arrow, two children and a sliver of a third captioned 'a little over two', then a bold line sweeps across with a 2.1 badge labelled replacement level.

scenes.vo: enough, on average, for a woman to be replaced by a daughter who survives to childbearing age.
scenes.visual: A mother, then a daughter that pops in on 'daughter' and a heart on 'survives' ('a daughter who survives to childbearing age'), under the pill REPLACED BY A DAUGHTER.

scenes.vo: Stay below that line for long enough,
scenes.visual: A solid blue card that lands as the narrator says 'for long enough': THE KEY WORDS and LONG ENOUGH in yellow.

scenes.vo: and if nobody moves in from elsewhere, a country's population eventually starts to shrink.
scenes.visual: A three-rung ladder of generations pops in beside the uncle, four people, then three, then two: each rung has one fewer, with no numbers, under the pill NO ONE MOVES IN.

scenes.vo: One survey below two point one does not mean a population is shrinking. The key words are "long enough".
scenes.visual: A single calendar page (one survey) pops in, then a big clock (time) on 'key', and the pill LONG ENOUGH lands on 'long' to repeat the key words the card showed.

scenes.vo: Every figure for India and its states comes from the National Family Health Survey,
scenes.visual: The map of India and its states fills in again as the source of every figure.

scenes.vo: conducted by the health ministry with the International Institute for Population Sciences.
scenes.visual: In a school set a hospital icon pops in on 'health' (the ministry) and a school icon on 'Institute' (IIPS), under the pill HEALTH MINISTRY + IIPS.

scenes.vo: The sixth round, NFHS-6, covered nearly six point eight lakh households. We use its fact sheets, which are provisional.
scenes.visual: The NFHS-6 map again, with its legend headed NFHS-6 fact sheets (provisional): the sixth round's data as one picture.

scenes.vo: The counts and comparisons are our own arithmetic. We will say so when we go further.
scenes.visual: The uncle on the right beside a balance and a notebook; the pill OUR OWN ARITHMETIC lands as the narrator says it, the hedge made visible.

scenes.vo: Let us follow India's own line. In the first round, in nineteen ninety-two ninety-three, it was three point four.
scenes.visual: The uncle opens the chapter with a calendar and a circled badge: India's rate in the first round, 3.4.

scenes.vo: In NFHS-3, in twenty oh-five oh-six, it was two point seven. In NFHS-4, in twenty fifteen sixteen, it was two point two,
scenes.visual: A flat line chart draws India's rate at NFHS-3 (2.7) and NFHS-4 (2.2) with the 2.1 replacement line just beneath the second dot.

scenes.vo: just above the line. In NFHS-5, in twenty nineteen twenty-one, it fell to two point zero.
scenes.visual: The chart now follows the dot from just above the line down through it to NFHS-5 (2.0), with a hand-drawn circle at the crossing.

scenes.vo: That was the first NFHS round to put India below two point one.
scenes.visual: The uncle on the right; a big calendar pops in on 'first' under the pill FIRST ROUND BELOW THE LINE.

scenes.vo: NFHS-6, whose results the health ministry released on twenty-nine May twenty twenty-six, shows two point zero again.
scenes.visual: A hospital icon for the health ministry and a badge with NFHS-6's India figure, 2.0, under the pill RELEASED MAY 2026.

scenes.vo: India's rate stays below the line. But India is not one number.
scenes.visual: A solid blue card, NOT ONE in yellow: the turn from one national number to many.

scenes.vo: It has thirty-six states and union territories, and the NFHS-6 release covers thirty-five of them.
scenes.visual: A house, a hospital and a school stand for the places; a circled 35 pops on 'thirty-five', under the pill STATES AND UNION TERRITORIES.

scenes.vo: Manipur is not in the NFHS-6 release. Those thirty-five places live in very different demographic worlds.
scenes.visual: The map fills in with Manipur left hatched and noted 'not in NFHS-6 release', while the narrator says the 35 places live in very different worlds.

scenes.vo: Here is NFHS-6, state by state. Of the thirty-five places, thirty are at or below two point one.
scenes.visual: The map fills in two colours: the places at or below the replacement line in cool blue, the few above it in warm orange, with a legend.

scenes.vo: Twenty-eight are below it, and two, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, sit right on the line at two point one.
scenes.visual: Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan lift off the two-colour map: the two places that sit right on the line.

scenes.vo: At the bottom, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands read zero point nine,
scenes.visual: A village set with palm trees; a circled badge lands on 0.9 for the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, under the pill THE BOTTOM.

scenes.vo: the only place in the survey below one child per woman. Sikkim comes next, at one point zero.
scenes.visual: The map lifts the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Sikkim and a LOWEST card slides in listing both with their rates.

scenes.vo: A caution on the islands: their figure rests on about two thousand four hundred women, a small sample.
scenes.visual: The uncle on the right looks concerned among palm trees; the pill SMALL SAMPLE lands on 'small'.

scenes.vo: At the top, Bihar reads two point seven. Four places follow at two point two:
scenes.visual: A badge for Bihar, 2.7, then a second badge, 2.2, for the four places that follow, above a row of four little houses, under the pill THE TOP.

scenes.vo: Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Uttar Pradesh, and the island territory of Lakshadweep.
scenes.visual: The five places above the line lift off the map and a HIGHEST card slides in listing them.

scenes.vo: Only five places in the survey are above two point one.
scenes.visual: Five houses pop in one by one on 'only five places in the survey are above': a literal tally, no digits, under the pill ABOVE THE LINE.

scenes.vo: Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana in the south,
scenes.visual: The five southern states named in the sentence lift off the two-colour map.

scenes.vo: and Gujarat, Maharashtra and Goa in the west, all read one point nine or lower.
scenes.visual: Three pills (GUJARAT, MAHARASHTRA, GOA) pop in as named and a circled 1.9 'or lower' lands, under the pill THE WEST.

scenes.vo: Between the lowest, zero point nine, and the highest, two point seven, the gap is one point eight children per woman.
scenes.visual: The two ends of the map lift off, each with its card, LOWEST 0.9 and HIGHEST 2.7, and the gap between them is the story.

scenes.vo: Some places moved a lot between NFHS-5, in twenty nineteen twenty-one, and NFHS-6, in twenty twenty-three twenty-four.
scenes.visual: The chapter opens with the uncle between two calendars that pop in on 'NFHS-5' and 'NFHS-6', each tagged with its years, under the pill THE BIGGEST FALLS.

scenes.vo: Meghalaya fell from two point nine to two point two, the biggest fall in the survey.
scenes.visual: Two badges for Meghalaya, NFHS-5 2.9 and then NFHS-6 2.2 circled, under the pill MEGHALAYA.

scenes.vo: Back in NFHS-4 it read three point zero, so most of the fall since then came between NFHS-5 and NFHS-6.
scenes.visual: A slope line for Meghalaya across NFHS-4, NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 (3.0, 2.9, 2.2) shows how much of the fall came in the last step.

scenes.vo: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands fell from one point three to zero point nine, again a small-sample place.
scenes.visual: Two badges for the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, 1.3 then 0.9 circled, with the pill SMALL SAMPLE landing on 'small-sample'.

scenes.vo: Bihar, still the highest, fell from three point zero to two point seven.
scenes.visual: Back in the Bihar home of the cold open: badges for NFHS-5 (3.0) and NFHS-6 (2.7, circled), under the pill BIHAR: STILL THE HIGHEST.

scenes.vo: Arunachal Pradesh, Assam and Mizoram each fell by zero point three on the printed figures.
scenes.visual: Arunachal Pradesh, Assam and Mizoram lift off the map: the three places that each fell by about the same step.

scenes.vo: Those are rounded to one decimal, so read that as about zero point three.
scenes.visual: A balance pops in on 'rounded' beside a cautious uncle; the pill SO: ABOUT lands on 'about'.

scenes.vo: Bihar went from three point four, to three point zero, to two point seven.
scenes.visual: A line chart follows Bihar's three dots, 3.4, 3.0 and 2.7, down toward the 2.1 line.

scenes.vo: Assam went from two point two, to one point nine, to one point six.
scenes.visual: The same chart for Assam: 2.2, 1.9 and 1.6, crossing under the 2.1 line.

scenes.vo: Meghalaya, Bihar and Assam were each lower in every round.
scenes.visual: Three small line charts side by side, Meghalaya, Bihar and Assam, each lower at every survey.

scenes.act: What goes with fewer babies? Our analysis
scenes.vo: So what do the lower-fertility places have in common?
scenes.visual: A solid blue card asking the chapter's question, FEWER BABIES in yellow, the uncle peeking up in the corner.

scenes.act: What goes with fewer babies? Our analysis

spec.title: Our *analysis*, not the survey's.
spec.sub: Tested on the NFHS-6 fact sheet figures

scenes.vo: We tested two things ourselves, using figures in the same NFHS-6 fact sheets. This part is our analysis, not the survey's.
scenes.visual: A sunburst title card with the uncle: OUR ANALYSIS in red, 'not the survey's' under it: the hedge stated as a headline.

scenes.act: What goes with fewer babies? Our analysis
scenes.vo: First, the share of women aged fifteen to forty-nine with ten or more years of schooling.
scenes.visual: A school set with a woman and a girl; a big school icon pops in on 'ten or more years' under the pill FIRST: SCHOOLING.

scenes.act: What goes with fewer babies? Our analysis
scenes.vo: Second, the share of women aged twenty to twenty-four who were married before eighteen.
scenes.visual: A ring icon pops in on 'married' beside a grown woman, under the pill SECOND: MARRIED BEFORE EIGHTEEN.

scenes.act: What goes with fewer babies? Our analysis
scenes.vo: Across all thirty-five places, where more women had ten or more years of schooling,
scenes.visual: A woman and a school icon that pops in on 'women', under the pill ACROSS ALL THE PLACES.

scenes.act: What goes with fewer babies? Our analysis
scenes.vo: fertility tends to be lower. The correlation is minus zero point three six.
scenes.visual: A scatter of 35 dots (schooling against fertility) with a falling trend line; a correlation badge lands with -0.36 and the sticker 'Pattern, not proof'.

scenes.act: What goes with fewer babies? Our analysis

pills.text: TEN OR MORE YEARS OF SCHOOL

scenes.vo: In Kerala, eighty-seven percent of women had ten or more years of schooling,
scenes.visual: Two mothers stand side by side in one street, Kerala and Bihar, same set and same cast; a circled 87% lands over Kerala's mother for schooling.

scenes.act: What goes with fewer babies? Our analysis
scenes.vo: and three percent of women aged twenty to twenty-four were married before eighteen.
scenes.visual: The same street and the same two mothers; a circled 3% lands over Kerala's mother for marriage before eighteen.

scenes.act: What goes with fewer babies? Our analysis
scenes.vo: In Bihar, the figures are thirty-three percent and thirty-five percent.
scenes.visual: The same street and the same two mothers; now Bihar's mother gets the two badges, 33% for schooling and 35% for marriage before eighteen.

scenes.act: What goes with fewer babies? Our analysis
scenes.vo: For child marriage, the link is weaker: plus zero point two nine.
scenes.visual: The same scatter for child marriage: a rising, looser trend line and a correlation badge with +0.29.

scenes.act: What goes with fewer babies? Our analysis
scenes.vo: With only thirty-five places, a link that weak could partly be chance.
scenes.visual: A cautious uncle with a speech bubble 'CHANCE?' and a badge for the small number of places, 35, under the pill COULD PARTLY BE CHANCE.

scenes.act: What goes with fewer babies? Our analysis
scenes.vo: Next, compare with NFHS-5. On the same thirty-five places, the schooling link was minus zero point five two,
scenes.visual: A calendar for the earlier survey and a circled badge with the NFHS-5 schooling link, -0.52, under the pill COMPARE WITH NFHS-5.

scenes.act: What goes with fewer babies? Our analysis
scenes.vo: and the child marriage link was plus zero point four six. So both links are weaker in NFHS-6.
scenes.visual: A ring icon and a circled badge with the NFHS-5 child-marriage link, +0.46; the pill BOTH WEAKER NOW lands on 'weaker'.

scenes.act: What goes with fewer babies? Our analysis
scenes.vo: Part of that comes from one small island territory.
scenes.visual: Lakshadweep lifts off the map: the one small island territory behind part of the weakening.

scenes.act: What goes with fewer babies? Our analysis
scenes.vo: Lakshadweep, where eleven hundred fifty women were interviewed, is among the highest in schooling and reads two point two on fertility.
scenes.visual: Palm trees and a school: a badge for 1,150 women interviewed and a circled 2.2 fertility rate, under the pill LAKSHADWEEP.

scenes.act: What goes with fewer babies? Our analysis
scenes.vo: Leave it out, and the schooling link is minus zero point four six, against minus zero point five zero in NFHS-5.
scenes.visual: Two badges with the schooling link without Lakshadweep: -0.46 for NFHS-6 (circled) and -0.50 for NFHS-5, under the pill WITHOUT LAKSHADWEEP.

scenes.act: What goes with fewer babies? Our analysis
scenes.vo: So the link has softened a little. It has not disappeared.
scenes.visual: A balance beside the uncle, the pill SOFTENED, NOT GONE: the link has weakened but is still there.

scenes.act: What goes with fewer babies? Our analysis
scenes.vo: A word of caution. This is a pattern, not proof that one thing causes the other.
scenes.visual: A solid blue card, NOT PROOF in yellow, the uncle peeking up: the chapter's caution.

scenes.act: What goes with fewer babies? Our analysis
scenes.vo: Many other things differ between states, and we did not test them.
scenes.visual: The map again, a quiet reminder that many other things differ between places; its legend is headed 'Next: the twist'.

scenes.vo: Here is the twist. Between NFHS-4 and NFHS-5, of the thirty-three places that can be compared, Manipur included,
scenes.visual: A badge THE TWIST lands, then a circled 33 'places compared', under the pill MANIPUR INCLUDED.

badges.caption: fell by zero point three or more

scenes.vo: fourteen fell by zero point three or more on the printed figures.
scenes.visual: A big circled 14: the places that fell by 0.3 or more between NFHS-4 and NFHS-5, under the pill ON THE PRINTED FIGURES.

scenes.vo: None rose by that much. The other nineteen were about the same.
scenes.visual: A badge with 19 'about the same', the uncle on the right, under the pill NONE ROSE THAT MUCH.

scenes.vo: Two read slightly higher: Kerala, from one point six to one point eight,
scenes.visual: A single small line chart for Kerala from NFHS-4 (1.6) to NFHS-5 (1.8): a small step, tagged about the same.

scenes.vo: and Tamil Nadu, from one point seven to one point eight.
scenes.visual: The same small chart for Tamil Nadu, 1.7 to 1.8.

scenes.vo: NFHS-6 looks different. In sixteen of the thirty-five places, NFHS-6 is higher than NFHS-5.
scenes.visual: The turn of the film: the uncle's speech bubble says WAIT. UP? and a huge circled 16 lands with 'higher, by any amount', after a GUESS FIRST pill, with the camera pushing in.

scenes.vo: In twelve it is lower, and in seven it is the same.
scenes.visual: Two badges land beside the 16: 12 'lower' and 7 'the same', under the pill NFHS-6 VS NFHS-5.

scenes.vo: But look closer. In ten of those sixteen,
scenes.visual: A solid blue card, CLOSER in yellow: the second turn.

scenes.vo: the difference is just zero point one, and we treat that as about the same.
scenes.visual: A balance barely tilting beside the uncle: the pill A TINY STEP, then ABOUT THE SAME lands on 'about'.

scenes.vo: On the printed figures, six places are zero point three or more higher,
scenes.visual: The map pulses the six places that rose by 0.3 or more in warm orange rings while the others stay grey; the legend says all sample sizes are included.

scenes.vo: and six are zero point three or more lower.
scenes.visual: The six places that fell by 0.3 or more lift off the map (Meghalaya, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Mizoram) under the legend heading 'Lifted: the biggest falls'.

scenes.vo: Among places with bigger samples, the largest rise is Jammu and Kashmir: one point four in NFHS-5, one point eight in NFHS-6.
scenes.visual: A line chart with two dots for Jammu and Kashmir, 1.4 and 1.8, the largest rise among the places with bigger samples.

scenes.vo: Nagaland fell by a full child per woman between NFHS-4 and NFHS-5, from two point seven to one point seven.
scenes.visual: A line chart for Nagaland: 2.7 down to 1.7, a full child per woman, against the 2.1 line.

scenes.vo: In NFHS-6 it reads two point zero, about zero point three higher.
scenes.visual: A slope line for Nagaland's three surveys, 2.7, 1.7 and 2.0: the third dot rises about 0.3.

scenes.vo: A few small places also show jumps,
scenes.visual: The five small-sample places lift off the map: the places the narrator leaves out.

scenes.vo: but their samples run from about eight hundred to two thousand two hundred women, so we leave them out.
scenes.visual: A cautious uncle beside five little houses; the pills SMALL SAMPLES and LEFT OUT (on 'leave').

scenes.vo: Kerala reads one point eight again, and Tamil Nadu one point seven. Both are about the same.
scenes.visual: Two small line charts, Kerala (1.6, 1.8, 1.8) and Tamil Nadu (1.7, 1.8, 1.7): flat, tagged about the same.

scenes.vo: So is India's fall levelling off? One survey cannot tell us.
scenes.visual: The uncle's speech bubble asks LEVELLING OFF? beside a clock and a single calendar page: one survey, one snapshot.

scenes.vo: The NFHS-6 numbers are provisional, and only a later survey can show
scenes.visual: The uncle on the right points at a new calendar page that pops in on 'later'; the pills PROVISIONAL and A LATER SURVEY land with the words.

scenes.vo: whether this is a turn or just noise.
scenes.visual: A solid blue card with the question the film leaves open: A TURN? OR JUST NOISE?, NOISE in yellow, the uncle peeking up.

scenes.vo: Why does this matter? The United Nations notes that in countries below replacement level, population ageing speeds up.
scenes.visual: The chapter opens in a clinic: a clock pops in on 'ageing', the pills WHY IT MATTERS and UNITED NATIONS.

scenes.vo: And if fertility keeps falling, then over the long run the share of people of working age shrinks,
scenes.visual: A street of working-age adults and a clock, under the pill WORKING AGE.

scenes.vo: and the share of older people grows.
scenes.visual: A father and two grandmothers that pop in on 'share' and 'older', under the pill OLDER PEOPLE.

spec.title: Kerala and Bihar: two age profiles
spec.sub: Share of people aged sixty or older
spec.notes: GAP: the age figures are three levels deep in figures.json (age_structure.Kerala.age60plus.nfhs6), so no FigRef can print them. Add flat tables age60plus and under15 shaped like school10, then add the badges listed in STORYBOARD.md section 7.

scenes.vo: NFHS-6 already shows different age profiles. In Kerala, twenty point seven percent of people are sixty or older.
scenes.visual: A sunburst title card with the uncle: Kerala and Bihar, two age profiles, the share of people aged sixty or older.

spec.notes: GAP: print age60plus for Bihar and India here once figures.json has a flat age60plus table (STORYBOARD.md section 7).

scenes.vo: In Bihar, eleven point five percent. For India as a whole, twelve point nine percent.
scenes.visual: One grandmother and a calendar; the pills BIHAR and INDIA AS A WHOLE land as named (no digits yet: the table is missing).

spec.notes: GAP: print under15 for Bihar and Kerala here once figures.json has a flat under15 table (STORYBOARD.md section 7).

scenes.vo: At the other end, thirty-five point six percent of people in Bihar are under fifteen, against twenty point three percent in Kerala.
scenes.visual: Two children; the pills BIHAR: UNDER FIFTEEN and KERALA land as named (no digits yet: the table is missing).

scenes.vo: The table shows how much, not why.
scenes.visual: A solid blue card that answers the film's question in four short lines (BELOW THE LINE? YES. SHRINKING? ONE SURVEY CAN'T SAY.), the uncle peeking up.

scenes.vo: So where does your state sit on the map,
scenes.visual: The NFHS-6 map one last time, its legend headed 'Where does your state sit?'.

scenes.vo: and what do you see in your own family? Tell us in the comments.
scenes.visual: The uncle points at the viewer beside a family; a heart pops in on 'family', under the pill YOUR STATE, YOUR FAMILY.

spec.question: Is India running out of babies? It depends on where you live.

scenes.visual: The closing scene: the uncle asks the film's question in a speech bubble, a subscribe button rings, the sources sit on a board, and an empty frame waits for YouTube's next-video element.
